observed.facings.png: Three offline scene renders on one scale. South: a tall timber leaf with diagonal braces and iron corner plates stands upright on the north bank of a dark rectangular pit. Two small turned-wood bollards sit on the south bank, each with a tan rope ellipse just above its head. Thin bits of rope ring show on either side of the leaf's base. East: a wide scene in which the raised leaf is seen edge-on as a thin vertical plank on the west edge of the pit. Two bollards stand on each bank, each with a horizontal rope ellipse lying beside it on the pit side. North: the leaf shows its plank back with iron bands, standing in the pit area. The north-bank bollards have rope ellipses just below their feet. The south-bank bollards have ellipses just above their heads.
observed.south.png: Raised leaf, rot S: a braced timber door stands upright from a hinge bar at the north edge of the pit. Behind its base, small slivers of rope ring poke out on both sides, so the north-bank coils are mostly hidden. On the south bank, two bollards stand about 30 px tall. Each has a smooth, closed tan rope ellipse (about 40x20 px) whose lower edge rests on the bollard's top, so it looks like a hoop or halo sitting on the bollard head. No rope run from bollard foot to ring is visible.
observed.east.png: Rot E: the leaf is edge-on, a thin vertical plank with iron bands and a cap, rising from the west pit edge. On the west bank, each bollard has a closed rope ellipse lying flat on the ground to its east (toward the pit), touching the bollard base. The east bank mirrors this, with the ellipses on the west side of the bollards. Every ellipse is outside the pit. They read as rope rings lying on the ground.
observed.north.png: Rot N: the leaf's back face (vertical planks, four iron bands, hinge bar at its foot) covers the middle of the pit. North-bank bollards have rope ellipses just south of and in front of their feet, which reads as a coil on the ground. South-bank bollards repeat the south.png arrangement: the ellipse sits over the bollard head and the bollard body draws over the ring's lower edge.
observed.scale.png: Context render of the LOWERED state, rot E. A plank deck with copper plates spans the pit. Taut ropes run from four bollards to the deck edges. A vanilla human beside it is about two bollard heights taller than a bollard. Bollards and ropes are small relative to the human, which looks plausible.
observed.assembled_1.png: Same picture as north.png (raised, rot N).
observed.assembled_2.png: Same picture as south.png (raised, rot S).
observed.assembled_3.png: Same picture as east.png (raised, rot E).
observed.assembled_4.png: Raised, rot W: mirror of rot E. The edge-on leaf stands at the east pit edge, and rope ellipses lie on the ground beside each bollard on the pit side. None are over the pit.
observed.assembled_5.png: Lowered, rot N (context only): the deck spans the pit vertically, and two taut ropes run from each bank's bollards to the deck ends.

CAMERA.seen: The rope rings are ellipses about 0.5 as tall as wide, consistent with lying in the ground plane under the building camera.

BORE.seen: Rope is solid. No pipe or hose bore is shown anywhere.

PORTS.seen: In rot E/W and on the north bank in rot N, the ring touches the bollard foot. On the south bank in rot N and rot S, the ring touches the bollard HEAD, about 30 px above the foot, with no rope run from the foot. It reads as attached at the top, not leaving the foot on the ground.

PORTS_DRAWN.seen: Each visible bollard has exactly one rope ring. The north-bank bollards in rot S are hidden by the leaf, but ring slivers show beside its base. No extra connectors.

LAYERS.seen: Rings behind a bollard (further north) are overdrawn by the bollard body. The north-bank coils in rot S are overdrawn by the raised leaf. Both are correct for depth.

ROTATIONS.seen: Same bollards, same tan rope rings and same palette in N/E/S/W. The 67% height spread comes from scene canvas shape (E/W landscape scene vs N/S portrait scene), not from a sprite size jump.

SIGNATURE.seen: The ropes read as smooth, closed single hoops (quoit rings), not as a slack rope coil winding a little over one turn with a tail running to the bollard foot. On the south bank in N/S the hoop sits on the bollard head like a halo.

MATERIAL.seen: Twisted tan strands read as hemp rope. The bollards read as turned wood with copper banding.

FOOTPRINT.seen: Each coil stays beside its bollard on the bank, never over the pit.

ALPHA.seen: Only composited scene renders on a deck/ground fill are given, so the rope sprite's own cut-out cannot be inspected. The code's 'real alpha present: False' refers to these composites. Nothing looks like a baked shadow or halo around the rope.

OURS.seen: Procedural rope from the mod's own render path (RM_DrawbridgeCableMath.Slack). Not donor art.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: 'Slack and disconnected' holds in E/W and on the north bank in rot N. On the south bank in rot N/S the ring rests on the bollard head, so it reads as a hoop hung on or floating over the post rather than rope slack on the ground. The leftover look of something standing above the bollard is what the redraw was meant to remove.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px/cell each ring would be about 10x5 px. A closed hoop that small reads as a dot or ring, not a coil, and the halo-on-bollard reading on the south bank gets stronger when shrunk.

concerns.evidence: In south.png and the lower bank of north.png, repeated in assembled_2 and assembled_1, the rope ellipses sit above the posts. Their lower edges meet the post heads while the post feet remain visibly below, making the rings read as elevated.
The lower-bank rings touch the tops of the bollards in the south and north views. No visible strand descends from those rings to the bollard feet.

Across the raised views, the ropes form regular closed oval outlines. Their closely spaced edges read as rope thickness; no distinct overlapping turn or loose terminal strand establishes a coil winding beyond one revolution.

The supplied renders visibly contain opaque brown backgrounds and dark pit rectangles, consistent with the reported absence of alpha. These intentional scene backgrounds prevent inspection of the rope asset's own transparency; an isolated rope render over transparency is missing.
